Under Dutch rules, overland transport to the Netherlands only needs the burial or cremation permit. Delays were not confirmed; the funeral director handles the process.
LU.authority: Civil registrar of the commune; Direction de la Santé, Division de l'Inspection sanitaire (Strasbourg laissez-passer)

documents: Transport permit for the body from the competent authority of the country of death (Strasbourg laissez-passer between party states)
If the country of death has no such authority: certificate stating the cause of death from a medical institution, doctor or law-enforcement body

From the USA (Latvian embassy guidance): apostilled medical cause-of-death certificate, death certificate and embalming certificate, plus a declaration that the deceased had no known infectious condition (or a removal permit) and that the coffin holds only the remains
Contact details of the Latvian funeral home that will receive the coffin
LV.coffin: Regulation No. 523, paras 7-8: hermetically sealed coffin filled with absorbent material (dry sawdust, fine wood shavings or peat), with a pressure-balancing and air-filtering device if needed. A wooden coffin needs walls of at least 20 mm when it contains a soldered zinc coffin (or one of another disintegrating material), or at least 30 mm when it is covered outside with soldered zinc (or other disintegrating material) plates. For transport the coffin goes in a solid wooden box that does not look like a coffin, marked 'handle with care'. No witness for the sealing is specified for incoming coffins.
LV.embalming: Latvian law does not require embalming for entry, but the Latvian embassy in the USA lists an embalming certificate (apostilled) for a coffin shipped from the US. Follow the departure country's rules.
LV.consular: No Latvian consular permit is required. Between Strasbourg states the laissez-passer suffices. Latvian missions (example: Washington) ask for the death, cause-of-death and embalming certificates with an apostille. For a death abroad, the Latvian Foreign Ministry advises informing the local police, the Latvian embassy or consulate and the insurer; consular duty line +371 26337711.
LV.arrival: The receiving Latvian funeral home collects the coffin; confirm airport and customs handling with it. Regulation 523 (para 18, in the chapter on infectious diseases) says a body is buried or cremated no earlier than 24 hours after death. Latvia's only crematorium is in Riga.
LV.private_aviation: Fly to Riga (or another Latvian airport with customs) with the receiving funeral home meeting the aircraft. Regulation 523 allows coffins by air in the luggage or cargo hold, inside a wooden box that does not look like a coffin, which a small cabin may not accommodate; check the cargo door size.
LV.export: To take a body out of Latvia you need a body transport permit from the Health Inspectorate (Veselibas inspekcija), which is also Latvia's declared Strasbourg authority since 2009. The application includes a medical certificate of cause of death with its ICD-10 code (or the death certificate showing it) and a funeral company's statement that the body is in a coffin meeting para 7 and that the coffin holds only the body and personal effects. The permit is completed in Latvian and one Council of Europe language. The Inspectorate refuses it if these requirements are not met. Transit through Latvia needs no Latvian permit. Death must be registered at the civil registry office within six working days.

documents: Written request stating the route of the body and the place of burial
Copy of the Moroccan electronic ID card (or other ID) of the deceased and of the applicant
Death certificate issued by the authorities of the country of death
Report (proces-verbal) of placing the body in a hermetically sealed coffin, issued by the competent authorities of the country of death
Certificate that the body is not contagious, from the health services of the country of death
Document from the judicial authorities of the country of death if the death was unnatural or suspected to be
MA.coffin: Hermetically sealed and sealed coffin, with an official sealing report from the country of death. Morocco's 2025 health and safety order describes a zinc coffin of at least 0.45 mm with a filter, fixed inside a sealed wooden coffin 30 mm thick, and requires transport coffins to meet the standard set on a health doctor's opinion.
MA.embalming: No general embalming requirement appears in the decree. For certain infectious diseases the 2025 order requires the body to be coffined without washing or embalming. Airlines may require embalming; confirm with the consulate and carrier.
MA.consular: The Moroccan consulate processes the entry authorisation on behalf of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and registers the death. That authorisation also counts as the transport permit inside Morocco. Translations into Arabic or French may be requested.
MA.arrival: Airport health services check the documents, then the body is released to the family or a funeral company. The burial permit is issued by the president of the communal council of the burial place on the basis of the entry authorisation. Muslim burial takes place quickly.
MA.private_aviation: The entry authorisation is requested with the route of the body, so the private flight and arrival airport should be stated in the request and match the authorisation. Land at an airport with health control and customs.
MA.export: Leaving Morocco: the exit authorisation is issued by the governor (amel) of the prefecture or province where the body is, on a request naming the destination country, with ID, a non-contagious certificate, the consent of the destination country's embassy or consulate, judicial authorisation for unnatural deaths, and a sealing report of the hermetic coffin drawn up by the national police or Royal Gendarmerie (Decree 2-22-218, art. 10). Files go to a one-stop desk at the communal hygiene office with a morgue. The King's Prosecutor orders an autopsy for non-natural deaths and deaths of foreigners. CMPF is cited as the only firm able to repatriate non-Muslim foreigners. Formalities usually take 2 to 3 days.
MA.authority: Moroccan Ministry of Foreign Affairs (consulates); governors for exits

documents: Authorisation for entry into France from the French embassy or consulate in the country of death
Death certificate from the country of death, with French translation if needed
Authorisation from the Minister of State of Monaco for the France-Monaco leg (1963 agreement; confirm how it applies to a body arriving from abroad)
MC.coffin: French rules require an airtight coffin (metal box) for air transport. The 1963 Franco-Monegasque agreement requires a hermetically sealed coffin when the journey exceeds 200 km, when more than 48 hours pass between encoffining and burial, for certain contagious diseases, or when the authorities order it; otherwise a 26 mm oak coffin with iron bands and a watertight lining.
MC.embalming: No Monegasque embalming rule was found; follow the departure country's and French rules.
MC.consular: Monaco is not a party to the Strasbourg or Berlin agreements. Because the flight lands in France, entry into France of a body from abroad is authorised by the French embassy or consulate in the country of death. Monaco's own consular requirements were not found.
MC.arrival: The coffin clears customs in France and is driven to Monaco. Under the 1963 agreement the Minister of State authorises transfers between metropolitan France and Monaco. Burial and civil registry formalities in Monaco were not verified: confirm with the Monaco funeral director and the Mairie.
MC.private_aviation: There is no airport in Monaco (heliport only). Fly to Nice Cote d'Azur or another French airport with customs, where French rules on human remains apply, and continue by hearse.
MC.export: For a body leaving Monaco for metropolitan France, the Minister of State authorises the transport (1963 Franco-Monegasque agreement), with a hermetic coffin beyond 200 km or 48 hours. For a flight abroad from Nice, French rules also apply; Monaco's procedure for destinations outside France was not published. Ashes are authorised the same way and must be in a protected urn.
MC.authority: Minister of State (Government of Monaco) for France-Monaco transfers; French embassy or consulate and French authorities for the arrival leg

documents: Laissez-passer for the corpse (Strasbourg Agreement states)
Death certificate from the country of death
From non-Strasbourg countries: documents to be confirmed with the Moldovan embassy or consulate
Passport of the deceased
MD.coffin: From Strasbourg states: a leak-proof coffin with absorbent material, as the Agreement requires. Moldovan rules for coffins from other countries were not verified. For shipments out of Moldova, the US Embassy reports that a galvanised casket is used and that a casket is treated as ordinary freight.
MD.embalming: According to the US Embassy, Moldova has no mandatory embalming rules except when a body is transported; bodies leaving Moldova must be embalmed. Whether Moldova requires embalming for an incoming body was not verified; follow the departure country's rules and confirm with the consulate.
MD.consular: If both countries are Strasbourg parties, the laissez-passer suffices (Moldova's own competent authority for issuing it is the Ministry of Health). Otherwise contact the Moldovan embassy or consulate in the country of death about certification and translation. Moldova applies the Agreement only on territory under government control (not Transnistria).
MD.arrival: Clearance at Chisinau airport and handover to a Moldovan funeral home. No maximum period before burial in Moldovan law.
MD.private_aviation: Chisinau is the main international airport. Moldova borders Ukraine, whose airspace is closed; check routing and any airspace restrictions near the border.
MD.export: Leaving Moldova: the body must be embalmed. US Embassy list: official death certificate, affidavit of funeral director and mortuary certificate, copy of autopsy certificate and copy of the passport. UK guidance list: civil registry death certificate (Public Services Agency, apostille via the Ministry of Justice if needed), doctor's death certificate with cause of death, embalming certificate and a certificate permitting transfer of the remains. A galvanised casket is used. Autopsy is mandatory for unknown or sudden deaths and, per UK guidance, for foreign nationals (can be waived by the regional prosecutor). The US Embassy reports an average of 10-14 days for return of remains. No crematorium (cremation in Odesa, Ukraine).
MD.authority: Ministry of Health (Strasbourg laissez-passer); Public Services Agency; Moldovan embassies and consulates

documents: Montenegrin conveyance (sprovodnica) from the Montenegrin embassy or consulate

Documents the funeral company submits for the conveyance (list not published; typically death certificate, cause-of-death certificate, embalming certificate, departure country transfer permit and passport): confirm with the embassy or consulate
ME.coffin: Not published for entry. Montenegro's export practice is a hermetically sealed coffin with a metal container (leak-proof); the same standard is expected.
ME.embalming: Not published for entry; plan embalming in the departure country. For export, embalming is described as essential for overseas transport (only at the Clinical Centre in Podgorica, within 72 hours of death).
ME.consular: Montenegro's government states that a conveyance is the document for transporting remains (coffin or urn) across borders, for burial in Montenegro or transit. The request is made to the Montenegrin embassy or consulate general (or an authorised foreign consular office) in the area of the deceased's last residence, usually by the funeral company, which provides the documentation; the officer checks it and issues the conveyance. Fee 20 or 25 EUR. The exact document list is not published.
ME.arrival: Clearance at Podgorica or Tivat airport and handover to a local funeral home; the transport must be accompanied by a registered funeral agency. Burial may not take place until 24 hours after death.
ME.private_aviation: No specific rules published for private flights carrying remains. Use Podgorica or Tivat, both international airports with customs.
ME.export: Leaving Montenegro: the death is registered with the Ministry of Interior registry office in the municipality of death. The funeral home obtains the death certificate, medical cause-of-death certificate, sanitary inspection certificates (Ministry of Health), embalming certificate, and the funeral home affidavit that the casket is hermetically sealed. Embalming only at the Clinical Centre in Podgorica, within 72 hours. No crematorium; cremation in Belgrade or Zagreb can take 5-10 days.
ME.authority: Montenegrin embassies and consulates (conveyance); Ministry of Health (sanitary inspection); Ministry of Interior (civil registry)

documents: Authorisation for entry from the French embassy or consulate in the country of death
Death certificate from the country of death
Other documents (medical certificate, embalming, sealing report) as requested by the consulate and the departure country
Name of the receiving funeral home
MF.coffin: For air transport an airtight coffin (metal box) is mandatory under French rules; in practice this is a soldered metal (usually zinc) lining inside a wooden coffin.
MF.embalming: France does not impose a single rule for incoming bodies; embalming or conservation care is normally required by the departure country and by carriers. Confirm with the consulate.
MF.consular: Under French rules, entry of a body from abroad into France is authorised by the French embassy or consulate in the country of death. France is a Strasbourg Agreement party, but whether a Strasbourg laissez-passer alone is accepted for this overseas collectivity was not confirmed: check with the consulate. Families bear all costs.
MF.arrival: The receiving funeral home takes charge at the airport. Burial or cremation deadlines in the overseas collectivity were not verified: check with the funeral home. Transfers between the collectivity and mainland France are authorised by the State's representative in the collectivity (towards mainland France) or by the prefect (from mainland France).
MF.private_aviation: Human remains on a private or charter flight need the same documents as airline cargo, travelling with the coffin, and the French airtight coffin rule applies to any air transport. The coffin must fit the aircraft's cargo door and cargo hold (a coffin never travels in the cabin). Saint Martin shares its island with Sint Maarten; Grand Case airport is small, so many flights use Princess Juliana airport on the Dutch side: confirm customs and the transfer across the island in advance.
MF.export: To send a body out of French territory, the funeral home obtains authorisation from the State's representative (prefect) for the place where the coffin is closed; for this collectivity that is the prefect delegate for Saint-Barthelemy and Saint-Martin (confirm locally). An airtight coffin is mandatory for air transport, and the destination country's consular requirements also apply.
MF.authority: French embassy or consulate abroad (entry); State representative, prefect delegate for Saint-Barthelemy and Saint-Martin (exit)

Coffinning certificate (attestation de mise en bière)

MG.coffin: Malagasy embassies require a coffin closing permit and a coffinning certificate, but publish no technical specification. Standard international practice: hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin in a wooden outer case.
MG.embalming: Not stated in the Malagasy embassy checklist; normally required by the sending country and airlines.
MG.consular: The Malagasy embassy or consulate issues the body or urn transport authorisation and transcribes the death (checklist published by the embassy in New Delhi, written for Malagasy nationals: copies of Malagasy IDs are requested). Files are lodged Monday to Friday, 09:30-12:00 (New Delhi). Fees and processing times are not published. Not a party to the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement.
MG.arrival: Remains arrive at Antananarivo (Ivato). The family must obtain the burial permit from the commune of burial before the authorisation is issued. Mortuary facilities are only in Antananarivo and limited; bodies for the regions travel by road. Confirm current health controls at arrival with the receiving funeral director.
MG.private_aviation: No rule specific to private flights carrying remains was found. The embassy checklist asks for flight details and an air waybill, so on a private flight provide the flight plan and confirm how the remains will be manifested. Land at an international airport with customs, normally Antananarivo.
MG.export: Deaths are confirmed by a doctor of the Municipal Bureau of Hygiene (BMH) or a CSB II health centre (or the head doctor in hospital) and registered with the civil registrar (acte de décès, in French). Police ask the coroner to carry out a post-mortem for unnatural, sudden or suspicious deaths (free; the family can object; report the day after the request at the soonest). The documents needed to send a body out of Madagascar are not published in official sources: the local funeral director and the destination country's consulate advise.
MG.authority: Malagasy embassy or consulate in the country of death; commune of burial in Madagascar

MN.coffin: Not published officially. International practice requires a hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin in an outer wooden case; confirm with the Mongolian consulate.
MN.embalming: Required for repatriation from Mongolia, with an embalming certificate; expected for incoming bodies. Confirm with the Mongolian consulate.
MN.consular: Mongolia is not a party to the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement. Contact the Mongolian embassy or consulate in the country of death about consular certification, legalisation or apostille and Mongolian translations.
MN.arrival: Not published officially. Expect customs and health clearance at Ulaanbaatar airport and handover to a local funeral service. The UK government states that a local burial cannot be arranged in Mongolia for a deceased British national (cremation is the only local option); confirm burial arrangements for Mongolian citizens with the local funeral service.
MN.private_aviation: No official rule specific to human remains on private aircraft was found. Plan arrival at an international airport with customs, border and sanitary-quarantine control, and have the handling agent confirm clearance of the coffin in advance.
MN.export: The hospital or local State Registration Office issues the death certificate in Mongolian (a certified translation may be needed); it should state the cause of death and that it was not an infectious disease, and police clearance may be needed if the death was caused by injuries of unknown origin. An autopsy at the National Institute of Forensic Science is required for foreign nationals and can take up to 1 month, during which the body is not released. The deceased's Mongolian visa must be cancelled with the Immigration Authority before release. Embalming is required, with an embalming certificate.
MN.authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Mongolia (consular department); National Institute of Forensic Science and Immigration Authority for exit

documents: Original or certified copy of the death certificate issued at the place of death, plus a photocopy (Health Bureau)

Photocopies of the deceased's and applicant's identity documents; Health Bureau request form
Mortuary laissez-passer (livre-trânsito mortuário) if more than 60 hours passed between death and entry; otherwise a Public Security Police (CPSP) relocation record (IAM, for temporary storage)
Declaration of relationship with the deceased and death registration from the Civil Registry, for temporary storage in a Macao cemetery (IAM)
Embalming certificate (confirm with the Health Bureau; required for public tomb storage)
MO.coffin: For temporary storage (IAM permit): lead coffin, and an IAM Sanitary Inspector must be notified to seal it. For storage in a public tomb, the lead coffin must be welded tight, coated outside with a 1.5 mm layer of quicklime and placed inside a wooden coffin. Confirm coffin rules for other destinations with the Health Bureau.
MO.embalming: Required for storage in a public tomb (IAM). For bodies leaving Macao, the Health Bureau requires an embalming certificate except for a coffin sent alone by vehicle to Zhuhai. No general embalming rule for incoming bodies is published; confirm with the Health Bureau.
MO.consular: No consular step specific to Macao is published. Macao is a Special Administrative Region of China; the mortuary laissez-passer (livre-trânsito mortuário) issued at the place of departure is required when the body arrives more than 60 hours after death. Foreign documents may need translation into Chinese or Portuguese; confirm with the Health Bureau.
MO.arrival: The Health Bureau Centre for Disease Prevention and Control checks the original sanitary handling declaration when the body arrives and issues the certificate on the next working day (stamp duty MOP 5). The IAM temporary storage permit takes 3 working days (fee MOP 2,000 per body over age 7, MOP 1,000 for age 7 or under, plus 10% stamp duty; storage up to 6 months). Health Bureau office: Avenida do Comendador Ho Yin, Qingmao Government Building, 18th floor; tel. +853 8504 1425; weekends and holidays by appointment.
MO.private_aviation: No rule specific to private flights carrying remains was found. The same Health Bureau and IAM documents apply whatever the aircraft; arrange the Health Bureau certificate and the sanitary inspector's attendance before landing at Macau International Airport, especially on weekends (appointment needed).
MO.export: A doctor (hospital death) or the coroner (police case) issues the death certificate. The death must be registered with the Civil Registry before the body can leave the mortuary. The Public Prosecution Office decides whether an autopsy is needed, which can delay release. The Health Bureau charges MOP 200 per day for frozen storage after the death certificate is issued. Repatriation costs about MOP 30,000 excluding air freight (UK guidance, 2020). Leaving Macao needs the Health Bureau Certificate of Medical Sanitation (issued next working day; the sanitary handling declaration is submitted before the coffin is sealed) and an embalming certificate except for a coffin sent alone by vehicle to Zhuhai.
MO.authority: Health Bureau (SSM) Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (Decree-Law 7/85, Despachos 02/SS/2018 and 05/SS/2018); Municipal Affairs Bureau (IAM); Public Security Police Force (CPSP)

documents: Death certificate stating the cause of death, with English translation if needed (required unless embalmed)

Burial-transit permit from the US state of death for domestic shipments (local CNMI requirement not verified)
MP.coffin: Federal rule: remains must be fully contained in a leak-proof container (double-layered puncture-resistant body bag, casket with certified leak-proof lining, or sealed metal transfer case). Hermetic sealing is not a federal requirement; airlines may require it.
MP.embalming: Not required by federal rules. Embalmed remains need no CDC permit; unembalmed remains need a death certificate or importer certification.
MP.consular: For US citizens who die abroad, the US embassy or consulate issues the consular report of death and mortuary documents. No CNMI-specific consular step.
MP.arrival: Remains must go directly to a licensed mortuary, cemetery or crematory. Local customs clearance applies (CNMI is outside the US customs territory). Death records are held by the Commonwealth Healthcare Corporation Health and Vital Statistics Office.
MP.pouch: Federal rules accept a double-layered, puncture-resistant, leak-proof body bag; airline and local funeral home acceptance must be confirmed.
MP.private_aviation: No rule specific to private flights carrying remains was found. A private aircraft arriving from abroad must land at an airport with customs (Saipan) and the remains must meet CDC rules on arrival.
MP.export: Local procedure not verified. Expect a death certificate from the Commonwealth Healthcare Corporation, a burial-transit permit and embalming by a local funeral home; the destination country's rules apply.
MP.authority: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (import); Commonwealth Healthcare Corporation (vital records)

documents: Local death certificate (transcription into French civil status advised, done by the consulate)
Medical certificate / non-contagious disease certificate as required by the departure country
Embalming (soins de conservation) certificate where required at departure
Authorisation to transport the body issued by the French embassy or consulate (or a mortuary laissez-passer from a Strasbourg Agreement state)
Coffin closing / sealing report
Receiving funeral director and burial or cremation arrangements in Martinique
MQ.coffin: For any air transport an airtight coffin is mandatory under French rules (in practice a soldered zinc lining inside a wooden coffin). A hermetic coffin cannot normally be cremated without being reopened, so plan cremation before departure.
MQ.embalming: No embalming rule for incoming bodies is stated in the official French guidance read; it is usually required by the departure country and by airlines for long journeys. Confirm with the French consulate.
MQ.consular: The French embassy or consulate in the country of death issues the authorisation to transport the body to France (including overseas departments) and can transcribe the death certificate. France is a party to the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement, so a laissez-passer from another party state is accepted. From mainland France, no consulate is involved: the prefect of the department where the coffin is closed authorises transport to Martinique.
MQ.arrival: The receiving funeral director in Martinique takes charge on arrival after customs and health formalities. Since Decree 2024-790 (10 July 2024), burial or cremation of a person who died abroad must take place no later than the 14th calendar day after the body enters France (Martinique is part of France); the prefect can grant exemptions.
MQ.private_aviation: Same documents as airline cargo; they travel with the coffin and are shown to customs and health officials at the arrival airport. The airtight zinc-lined coffin rule applies to any flight. Use an airport with customs (the main international airport) and arrange for the funeral director to meet the aircraft.
MQ.export: To send a coffin out of Martinique, the funeral director obtains authorisation from the prefect of Martinique (the department where the coffin is closed), for EU, non-EU and mainland France destinations alike. An airtight metal coffin is mandatory for air transport. The destination country's consular requirements also apply.
MQ.authority: French embassy or consulate abroad (entry); Prefect of Martinique (exit)

documents: Cadaver import permit issued by the Chief Medical Officer (apply before shipping)
Documentary evidence from the place of death that export of the body is lawfully authorised
Evidence of the cause of death (death certificate)
Evidence that the body is not likely to endanger health in Montserrat through disease
Consent of executors, administrators or relatives where practicable
Permit fee: $1,000 per body (Cadavers (Importation) (Fees) Regulations, S.R.O. 14/2013)
MS.coffin: The Chief Medical Officer sets the container type as a permit condition. The Act defines an impervious container as one hermetically sealed by gasket or soldered/welded metal, or a heat- or adhesive-sealed inner container inside an outer box. Customs may not open an impervious container without the Chief Medical Officer's approval. The definition also covers a heat- or adhesive-sealed plastic container inside an outer box, so a sealed pouch in a case may be acceptable if the permit allows it; confirm with the Chief Medical Officer.
MS.embalming: Not set by the Act. The Chief Medical Officer may impose conditions on the permit (container, keeping and disposal); confirm with the Chief Medical Officer whether embalming is required.
MS.consular: Montserrat has no consulates of its own; UK missions handle consular matters. No legalisation requirement is set by the Act, but the export authorisation and cause of death must be documented by the place of death.
MS.arrival: Customs at the port of entry checks the permit and may examine the container (not an impervious one without the Chief Medical Officer's approval). The permit fixes where the body is kept and how it is disposed of; burial still needs the registration formalities under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act. No customs duty is payable on the body.
MS.private_aviation: Montserrat's only airport (John A. Osborne) has a very short runway served by small turboprops; most business jets cannot land there, so a casket often travels by small aircraft or ferry via Antigua. Without a valid cadaver import permit the aircraft or vessel will be refused permission to land the body.
MS.export: No official procedure for sending a body out of Montserrat was found. Ask the local funeral home and the Ministry of Health and Social Services; the destination country's requirements apply.
MS.authority: Chief Medical Officer, Ministry of Health and Social Services, Government of Montserrat; Customs

MT.coffin: Soldered inner coffin of lead or zinc, or repatriation foil approved by the Environmental Health Directorate, packed inside a wooden coffin. The lid is screwed down, the screws are covered with tamper-proof seals and the coffin is wrapped in canvas or tarpaulin so the contents are not apparent. For infectious disease or advanced decomposition the body is normally placed in a body bag.
MT.embalming: A certificate of embalmment must accompany the remains (Port Health Services).
MT.consular: Malta is not a party to the Strasbourg Agreement. No Maltese consular permit is published; ask the Maltese embassy whether translation or apostille of the documents is required.
MT.arrival: Port Health Services clear the remains; a Maltese funeral director collects the coffin and a burial permit is needed for burial in Malta (Burials Regulatory Unit). There is no crematorium in Malta (UK guidance); a funeral director may arrange cremation in Sicily.
MT.private_aviation: Arrive at Malta International Airport and arrange the Port Health clearance in advance through the receiving funeral director (porthealth@gov.mt). The same documents and coffin standard apply as for airline cargo; out-of-hours clearance is possible at extra cost.
MT.export: Port Health Services supervise repatriations to, from or via Malta, with the same documents and coffin standard: death certificate, identity certificate, embalming certificate, burial permit (Burials Regulatory Unit) or coroner clearance form, and a health-authority certificate that the remains can be transported safely, in a soldered lead or zinc inner coffin (or approved repatriation foil) inside a wooden coffin. Fee 64 euros in office hours. Additional signed copies of the hospital death certificate are needed for repatriation. A magisterial inquiry into a death can take months and delay matters (UK guidance).
MT.authority: Port Health Services, Health Inspectorate (Environmental Health Directorate, Ministry for Health)

Exit permit from the country of death

Ministry of Health no objection to landing of the remains (unconfirmed)
MU.coffin: No official Mauritian specification found. Standard practice: hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin in a wooden outer case; confirm with the mission and airline.
MU.embalming: UK guidance states that in Mauritius embalming is compulsory for delayed burial or repatriation, and that unembalmed bodies must be buried within 24 hours. Incoming remains should be embalmed.
MU.consular: The Mauritian mission reportedly collects the documents and forwards them to the Ministry of Health, which issues the no objection to landing (non-official source). Not a party to the Strasbourg Agreement 1973, so a mortuary laissez-passer alone is not enough.
MU.arrival: Remains are cleared at Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam International Airport and released to the family's funeral director. If not embalmed, burial within 24 hours.
MU.private_aviation: No rules specific to private flights carrying remains were found. Land at SSR International Airport and carry the original documents and Ministry clearance.
MU.export: UK guidance: unless a doctor certifies a natural death, police seek a magistrate's authority for a post-mortem, normally within 24 hours. Embalming (arterial) is compulsory for repatriation and allows more than 30 days before transport. A local funeral director arranges documentation. Polish consular guidance lists: permit for burial abroad issued by local authorities, certificate of cause of death, embalming certificate and certificate of no sanitary objection for body transport. Suspicious deaths may lead to a judicial inquiry.

Deceased's home address in Malawi (village, Traditional Authority, district)
Authority letter to import human remains issued by the Malawi mission
MW.coffin: No Malawian coffin specification is published. Airlines and sending countries normally require a hermetically sealed (zinc-lined) coffin in an outer case; confirm with the airline.
MW.embalming: Required: an embalming certificate is on the Malawi mission's import checklist.
MW.consular: Malawi missions issue an authority letter to import human remains (published by the Consulate General in Sandton, South Africa). The High Commission in London provides documentation only when proper documents are lacking (covering letter, copies of death certificate and passport or birth certificate, funeral director documents) and gives no financial support. Malawian death certificates can be apostilled via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Malawi is not a party to the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement.
MW.arrival: Remains arrive at Lilongwe (Kamuzu) or Blantyre (Chileka) international airports and are released to the consignee named in the mission file after customs clearance. The mission checklist requires the deceased's home village, Traditional Authority and district. Temperature-controlled mortuary storage may not be available in rural areas (UK guidance).
MW.private_aviation: No rule specific to private flights carrying remains is published. Land at Lilongwe or Blantyre (customs and health services) with the mission's authority letter and original documents on board, and the consignee waiting.
MW.export: UK guidance: the death is registered with the National Registration Bureau based on the district hospital's death report. Airlines usually require a post-mortem and embalming for repatriation; post-mortems are done by government hospital pathology units. A funeral director usually needs the original burial permit, the embalming certificate, the death registration or certificate, a certificate permitting transfer of the remains and sometimes a passport copy.
MW.authority: Malawi diplomatic missions (Ministry of Foreign Affairs); National Registration Bureau

Transit permit for the body issued in the country of death
Embalming certificate
Certificate of no contagious disease
Mexican consular visa on the documents
Passport or ID of the deceased
MX.coffin: The consular pages consulted do not specify the coffin. In practice a sealed coffin prepared for international air transport is used; confirm the exact specification with the Mexican consulate and the airline.
MX.embalming: An embalming certificate is required for a body (not for cremated remains).
MX.consular: Original documents with Spanish translation are presented to the Mexican consulate with jurisdiction over the place of death, which visas them; the Seattle consulate states this visa is free of charge. The death certificate must be apostilled. Requirements vary slightly between consulates; Mexican consulates may give limited financial help to families in need, paid directly to the funeral home.
MX.arrival: The receiving Mexican funeral home presents the visaed documents and collects the coffin, then arranges burial or cremation under state law. Burial deadlines and local permits are set by the state civil registry and health authorities; confirm with the receiving funeral home.
MX.private_aviation: A private flight must clear immigration, customs and health at an international airport of entry in Mexico. The consular-visaed originals must travel with the coffin. Confirm with the handling agent that customs and health authorities are informed in advance.
MX.export: In Mexico the funeral director registers the death at the local Civil Registry (a medical certificate from the hospital or doctor is needed first; after violent or accidental deaths the police provide it) and obtains the civil registry death certificate, an embalming certificate and a certificate permitting transfer of the remains, then meets the destination's requirements (for the US, CDC leak-proof container rules). Post-mortems are carried out by forensic doctors; their reports can take several months, longer if there is a criminal investigation. Federal health permit details were not verified on an official page.

documents: Ministry of Health import permit or clearance under Act 342 regulations (confirm with the Malaysian mission)
Death certificate from the country of death stating the cause of death (English or Malay translation advisable)
Burial or transit permit / exit permit from the country of death
Embalming certificate and coffin sealing certificate (expected; confirm with the mission)
Passport or identity card of the deceased
Air waybill and airline release documents
MY.coffin: No published Malaysian specification was found. Airlines and IATA practice call for a hermetically sealed, zinc-lined coffin in a wooden outer case; confirm with the Malaysian mission.
MY.embalming: Not specified in an accessible official Malaysian source for incoming remains; embalming is normally required by the country of departure and by airlines.
MY.consular: No official Malaysian consular procedure for incoming remains was found online; confirm with the Malaysian embassy or high commission in the country of death. Malaysia is not a party to the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement.
MY.arrival: Expect health and customs clearance at the arrival airport before release to the receiving funeral service; the exact Ministry of Health inspection procedure is not published on an official page we could read. Under Act 342, if an infectious cause of death is suspected an authorised officer may order the body examined and give directions on burial or cremation.
MY.private_aviation: No rule specific to private flights was found. Land at an international airport with health and customs staff (for example KLIA) and confirm the Ministry of Health import requirements in advance through the handling agent.
MY.export: For a death outside hospital a post-mortem may be carried out; the hospital issues a Medical Certificate of Cause of Death and the police issue a burial permit, both free of charge. The death is registered with the National Registration Department (JPN) within seven working days of those documents, using them and the original passport (Australian High Commission). Repatriation needs a local death certificate, a certificate of embalming and a certificate giving permission to transfer the remains; some hospitals ask for a letter of no objection from the deceased's embassy (UK guidance). Export of human remains is also regulated under Act 342.
MY.authority: Ministry of Health Malaysia (Act 342) with Royal Malaysian Customs

documents: Death certificate (French translation advisable; transcription into French civil status recommended for French citizens)
Medical certificate of death / certificate of non-contagion
Body transport authorisation from the French embassy or consulate (from abroad), or prefectoral order (from mainland France)
Coffin closing/sealing report (procès-verbal de mise en bière)
Embalming certificate where required by the departure country or airline
NC.coffin: Local rule (délibération n° 35 of 7 March 1958, art. 120): for any transport outside urban limits the body is placed between two layers of absorbent, disinfectant material in a metal coffin welded until watertight, itself enclosed in a hard-wood coffin with walls 27 mm thick held by iron bands, the operation being done in the presence of the police commissioner or his delegate or the gendarmerie brigade commander. The New Caledonia competition authority notes that in practice air and sea transport therefore uses a welded zinc coffin inside a wooden coffin. Where burial is delayed, the wooden coffin must be at least 4 cm thick (art. 123).
NC.embalming: Not required by New Caledonian law: conservation care (thanatopraxy) is not regulated in New Caledonia and is rarely requested; only a few funeral firms offer it. Embalming is normally required by the departure country and the airline.
NC.consular: French consular services can issue an authorisation to transport the body or ashes so the remains leave the foreign country legally (diplomatie.gouv.fr). From mainland France, transport to New Caledonia needs a prefectoral order from the prefect where the coffin is closed, not a mortuary laissez-passer (Strasbourg/Berlin laissez-passer do not cover New Caledonia). Families pay all costs.
NC.arrival: The casket arrives at Nouméa-La Tontouta and is collected by a local funeral home after customs and health clearance. Transport outside urban limits needs the agreement of the doctor who issued the death certificate and is refused if death was due to a listed contagious disease (art. 120). Transport of a body to another commune needs a burial permit with the agreement of the receiving municipality (art. 121). Burial cannot take place less than 24 hours after death (art. 117). Cemetery rules are set by each commune (Nouméa has its own cemetery regulations). Inter-island transport of caskets is done by the Betico ship or Air Loyauté.
NC.private_aviation: No rule specific to private or charter flights was found. Local law requires the welded metal coffin in a hard-wood outer coffin for any transport outside urban limits, so a pouch or unsealed casket is not suitable. Arrive at Nouméa-La Tontouta (international airport with customs and health services) and have the funeral home in Nouméa confirm clearance before departure.
NC.export: Leaving New Caledonia: the transport needs the agreement of the doctor who certified the death (refused for listed contagious diseases), and the body must be in a welded watertight metal coffin inside a hard-wood coffin 27 mm thick with iron bands, sealed in the presence of the police or gendarmerie (délibération n° 35 of 1958, art. 120). Transports to foreign territories follow the rules of the destination country (art. 124). Entry into mainland France from New Caledonia is made on an authorisation from the French State representative (CGCT art. R. 2213-23, as cited by the New Caledonia competition authority). Typical delay is not published; confirm with the funeral home.
NC.authority: French consular network (entry from abroad); Government of New Caledonia (DASS) and communes for local funeral rules

Burial transit permit or certificate for shipping the body out of the country of death
Non-communicable disease letter or certificate from a coroner, medical examiner or health agency
Notarised embalmer's affidavit or embalming certificate
Notarised funeral home letter confirming a hermetically sealed metal casket containing only the remains
