Funeral home request letter to the mission and contact details of the receiving party in Nigeria
Mission fee and prepaid return envelope
NG.coffin: A hermetically sealed metal casket is required (Atlanta consulate list), confirmed by a notarised funeral home letter; the Ottawa High Commission asks for a funeral director's statement that the casket contains only the remains.
NG.embalming: Embalming is required, evidenced by a notarised embalmer's affidavit or embalming certificate.
NG.consular: After the Federal Ministry of Health waiver is granted, the Nigerian embassy, high commission or consulate checks the file and issues a letter (permission) for shipment of human remains. Fees vary by mission: 50 USD in Atlanta; 50 CAD per page plus a 50 CAD administrative fee in Ottawa, plus a 5,000 naira international waiver fee payable to Port Health Services. Ottawa quotes 10 business days; Atlanta gives no processing time.
NG.arrival: Arrival-side formalities (Port Health and customs clearance) are not detailed on the mission pages consulted; confirm with the receiving funeral home and the Nigerian mission. Carry the waiver, mission letter and original documents with the casket.
NG.private_aviation: The Port Health waiver and mission letter are required whatever the aircraft. Confirm the arrival airport and its Port Health and customs arrangements with the Nigerian mission before departure, and keep the waiver, mission letter and original documents with the casket.
NG.export: UK government guidance for taking a body out of Nigeria lists the death certificate, a death certificate from the National Population Commission, permission to remove the body issued by a coroner, the passport of the deceased and an infection-free declaration from the Ministry of Health; rules vary by location. The body must be embalmed (usually after any post-mortem) and placed in a metal casket. Cremation of a foreign national is possible.
NG.authority: Federal Ministry of Health, Port Health Services (Abuja); Nigerian diplomatic mission in the country of death

documents: Strasbourg states: laissez-passer issued by the competent authority of the country of death
Berlin Agreement states: the Berlin Agreement document (accepted by the civil registrar)
Other countries: declaration from the competent authority of the departure country naming the deceased and the destination
Belgium/Luxembourg overland: burial or cremation permit of the municipality of death
Death certificate (usually travels with the laissez-passer; confirm with the receiving funeral director)
NL.coffin: From Strasbourg Agreement states the coffin must meet articles 6 and 7 of that agreement (impermeable coffin with absorbent material; confirm the sealing standard with the departure funeral director). From Belgium, Luxembourg and non-Strasbourg countries a watertight coffin is required (Besluit op de lijkbezorging art. 12).
NL.embalming: No Dutch embalming requirement for incoming bodies; follow the departure country's rules. In the Netherlands embalming is generally prohibited, but the ban does not apply to bodies sent abroad.
NL.consular: From Strasbourg states no consular step is needed. From other countries the declaration of the departure country's competent authority is required; ask the Dutch embassy whether legalisation is needed.
NL.arrival: The laissez-passer, permit or declaration is presented to customs. The civil registrar of the municipality where burial or cremation will take place grants the permit on that document and keeps it. Burial or cremation normally within 6 working days of death; if the body arrives too late, as soon as possible after arrival. Transport by a hearse registered with the RDW.
NL.private_aviation: Present the laissez-passer or declaration to Dutch customs on arrival, so use an airport with customs and have the receiving funeral director and an RDW-registered hearse meet the aircraft. The coffin must fit the aircraft's cargo door and cargo hold (a coffin never travels in the cabin).
NL.export: The mayor of the municipality where the death was registered issues the laissez-passer for transport to Strasbourg states; for other countries a declaration of the competent authority naming the deceased and destination is used. If a non-natural death cannot be ruled out, the public prosecutor must give permission before transport, and embalming needs prosecutor consent. Embalming is permitted for bodies sent abroad.
NL.authority: Civil registrar (burgerlijke stand) of the municipality of burial; mayor of the municipality of death for exports

documents: Death certificate from the country of death (ask the Norwegian embassy whether legalisation or apostille is needed)
Transport documents or laissez-passer issued in the country of departure
Documents issued by the Norwegian embassy or consulate for the repatriation
Cause of death, ideally disclosed only to the municipal physician at the place of receipt
Body marked with name, date of birth and date of death
NO.coffin: Norwegian regulation FOR-1998-04-03-327 (§ 3-2) requires a packaging method approved by the Directorate of Health, unless treaties, airlines or receiving or transit countries require otherwise. The official commentary states that a metal inner coffin is required for transport to and from countries outside the Nordic region; a body bag may be used between Nordic countries. The body must be marked with the deceased's name, date of birth and date of death (§ 4-1). No Norwegian witness to sealing is required by the regulation.
NO.embalming: Not required by Norwegian rules for entry. Embalming falls under the general hygiene rules of the regulation; there is no transport-specific embalming rule.
NO.consular: The Norwegian embassy or consulate in the country of death issues the necessary documents for bringing the coffin home; the family arranges the transport itself with a local funeral company or insurer. The death is then recorded in the Norwegian population register by the Tax Administration. Ask the embassy whether the foreign death certificate must be legalised or apostilled.
NO.arrival: The recipient (usually a Norwegian funeral home) must collect the coffin as soon as possible after arrival (§ 3-3). Where possible only the municipal physician at the place of receipt is told the cause of death. If a serious infectious disease makes re-coffining risky, it must be done at a forensic institute or hospital pathology department.
NO.private_aviation: No Norwegian rule specific to private aircraft carrying human remains was found. The general packaging, marking and documentation rules of FOR-1998-04-03-327 apply. Norway is in Schengen but outside the EU customs union, so a flight from outside Schengen must land at an airport with border and customs control.
NO.export: Norwegian rules apply until the body leaves Norway. The sender must use packaging approved by the Directorate of Health unless the destination, transit country, airline or a treaty requires otherwise; the commentary requires a metal inner coffin outside the Nordic region. Where required, death documents for transport abroad are obtained from the police. Some destinations require embalming and an embalming certificate. The local district court (tingrett) issues the death certificate; sudden or unexpected deaths require a forensic autopsy, usually decided by the police prosecutor.
NO.authority: Norwegian Directorate of Health (packaging rules); Norwegian embassies and consulates; police (export documents)

documents: Copy of the death certificate
Copy of the deceased's passport
Embalming certificate (London)
Certificate of freedom from infection / no quarantinable disease from the local health authority
Coroner's certificate (London); police report for unnatural or accidental deaths (US)
Funeral director's declaration (London); burial transit permit (US)
Next of kin's application naming the receiver in Nepal (in the US, online through Nepal's Department of Consular Services or a local authorisation letter)
No Objection Letter from the Nepalese embassy
NP.coffin: The Nepalese embassy pages give no coffin specification. Confirm the casket and outer case requirements with the airline.
NP.embalming: The Nepalese Embassy in London requires an embalming certificate; the Washington embassy list does not mention one. Confirm with the embassy handling the file.
NP.consular: The Nepalese embassy issues a free No Objection Letter: the same day in London, 3 to 4 business days in Washington (applications through a licensed funeral shipping company). Document lists differ between missions, so check with the embassy in the country of death.
NP.arrival: The remains arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu, for the receiver named in the application. Cremation is the norm in Nepal and burial is used by some communities. Customs and health clearance steps on arrival are not published; confirm with the receiver and embassy.
NP.private_aviation: No official guidance on private flights carrying remains was found. Kathmandu (Tribhuvan) is the main international airport. Confirm aircraft permissions and arrival clearance with the operator before departure.
NP.export: From Nepal, autopsies are mandatory for unnatural deaths and are also done for insured remains to be repatriated; foreign nationals are autopsied at the Department of Forensic Medicine, Institute of Medicine, Kathmandu, usually within 24 hours, free of charge. A death certificate is usually available right after the autopsy. The post-autopsy death certificate and an embalming certificate are needed for the body to clear customs and immigration. Through Kathmandu funeral agents, repatriation usually takes about 1 to 10 days; via agents in India it can take 4 to 5 weeks. Refrigeration costs NPR 2,500 per day.
NP.authority: Nepalese embassy/consulate; Department of Consular Services, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Nepal

documents: Certified death certificate stating the cause of death, in English
Medical letter that the death was not due to an infectious or contagious disease (practice; not set by the Act for entry)
Embalming and casket sealing certificates (practice; not confirmed for entry)
Copy of the deceased's passport
Burial application to the cemetery Authority in the prescribed form, with a burial certificate from the Nauru Police Force (s. 19 of the 2017 Act)
NR.coffin: Not set for entry. Section 10 of the 2017 Act requires a body that died of an infectious or contagious disease to be sealed in a body bag and taken directly to burial or cremation. A sealed casket with an embalmed body is the safe choice for transport.
NR.embalming: Not required by the Act for entry. For leaving Nauru, section 13 requires a health practitioner's certificate that the remains are medically preserved and fit for transport, so embalming is effectively required on export.
NR.consular: No consular transfer permit is published. Nauru has few missions abroad (e.g. a High Commission in Suva and a consulate in Brisbane); ask the nearest one.
NR.arrival: Arrival at Nauru International Airport. Under section 12 the person in control must dispose of human remains within 24 hours, and section 10 requires the death to be registered with the Registrar of Births, Deaths and Marriages before disposal (the Registrar may be notified of deaths abroad of Nauruans and residents). Burial only in a designated burial ground between 7 am and 6 pm unless the Authority approves; since 2025 the President may permit burial at a residence or other place.
NR.private_aviation: Nauru International Airport is the only airport, served mainly by Nauru Airlines. Private aircraft need prior landing permission, and escorts need Nauruan visas. No rule specific to human remains on private flights was found.
NR.export: Section 13 of the Funeral Burial and Cremation Act 2017: no removal of remains from Nauru without (a) a health practitioner's certificate of death, (b) a death certificate from the Registrar of Births, Deaths and Marriages, (c) a health practitioner's certificate that the remains are medically preserved and capable of being transported, and (d) any conditions set by regulations. The remains must be transported within 6 hours of being received from the hospital. Ashes leave only with Authority approval, a sealed container, an Authority certificate and Quarantine Section clearance (s. 50).
NR.authority: Department of Health; Registrar of Births, Deaths and Marriages; burial ground Authority (Funeral Burial and Cremation Act 2017)

documents: Death certificate
Freight documents (air waybill or arrival notice)
Copy of the importer's photo ID
Embalming certificate and export permit required by the country of death and airline
NZ.coffin: No New Zealand-specific casket standard was found on official pages; a hermetically sealed coffin meeting airline and IATA requirements is normally used.
NZ.embalming: Not set as a New Zealand import requirement in official pages consulted; usually required by the country of departure and the airline.
NZ.consular: NZ Customs and MFAT pages do not mention any consular legalisation for entry; confirm with the funeral director. NZ embassies and MFAT can advise families, give funeral director contacts and certify copies of documents (fees charged), but cannot pay repatriation costs.
NZ.arrival: Customs clearance can be done by the post or freight service, or by emailing scanned documents to Customs; urgent after-hours clearance can be requested. A New Zealand funeral director collects the casket. The local death certificate travels with the body.
NZ.private_aviation: No Customs guidance specific to a casket on a private aircraft was found. Customs says remains carried by a traveller need no Customs clearance, but confirm with NZ Customs and arrange border and biosecurity clearance at the arrival airport before departure.
NZ.export: For remains sent out of New Zealand for interment, the freight forwarder or airline usually handles Customs formalities and no export entry is required. The funeral director arranges the death documents, embalming and a sealed casket to meet the destination country's and airline's rules.

documents: Death certificate (and death summary or autopsy certificate where applicable)
Passport of the deceased
Embalming certificate
No-objection certificates from the authorities of the country of death (e.g. foreign ministry, municipality, police)
No-objection certificate from the Omani embassy or consulate
Bill of lading / air waybill
OM.coffin: The transport company prepares the coffin and hands it to the carrier (Omani consulate Mumbai); the consulate publishes no coffin specification for entry. For bodies leaving Oman, UK guidance states that embalming and a zinc-lined coffin are required. Confirm specifications with the airline.
OM.embalming: An embalming certificate is part of the Omani consulate's checklist for bodies sent to Oman, and embalming is required for remains leaving Oman (gov.uk; Indian Embassy Muscat).
OM.consular: The Omani embassy or consulate is contacted by the accompanying person or a first-degree relative, confirms identity, obtains local approvals, liaises with Oman Air and issues its no-objection certificate. Oman is not a party to the Strasbourg Agreement.
OM.arrival: In Oman the family receives the body with the transport company's bill of lading and their ID, and checks they receive the original passport, municipal certificate, police or foreign affairs certificate, death summary and the consulate's NOC. Hearses can be arranged by region. Muslim burial normally follows quickly.
OM.private_aviation: No official rule specific to private or charter flights carrying human remains was found; Omani consulates route citizens' remains via Oman Air cargo. Confirm arrival clearance with the Omani mission before departure.
OM.export: The death is reported to the police and registered with the Royal Oman Police civil status office; post-mortems are carried out at the ROP police mortuary in Muscat, and Salalah cases need prior approval and an appointment before being taken to the ROP Qurum mortuary. The sponsor arranges embalming (ROP hospital, Qurum, or Khoula Hospital), coffin sealing and cargo booking; the home embassy issues its NOC and cancels the passport. Certificates of embalming, freedom from infectious disease (quarantine) and coffin sealing are required; documents go to the cargo office at Seeb. Indicative costs per the Indian Embassy: embalming RO 100-123, casket RO 180-200, cargo handling about RO 77.
OM.authority: Omani embassy/consulate abroad (Ministry of Foreign Affairs); Royal Oman Police (exit)

documents: Original death certificate
Original health certificate
Notarised transit permit
Notarised embalming certificate
Ashes instead: original death certificate, notarised cremation certificate and notarised burial-transit permit
PA.coffin: Not specified by the consulate. Panamanian funeral directors use a special casket for international transport (FCDO). Confirm casket requirements with the consulate and the airline.
PA.embalming: Embalming is expected: the consulate's list for a body (as opposed to ashes) requires a notarised embalming certificate.
PA.consular: The Panamanian consulate processes each document (Washington consulate: USD 30 per document, paid by money order, originals mailed with a prepaid return envelope). The consulate page does not mention apostilles or translations; check with the consulate covering the place of death.
PA.arrival: Arrival formalities are not published by the consulate; confirm customs and health clearance and collection with a funeral home in Panama. Burial in a government cemetery needs permission, usually obtained by an undertaker (FCDO).
PA.private_aviation: No specific Panamanian rule for private flights carrying remains was found. Carry the consulate-processed originals with the coffin, check that the coffin fits the aircraft, and confirm customs and health clearance at the arrival airport before departure.
PA.export: Leaving Panama: the death is registered with the Direccion Nacional del Registro Civil (Tribunal Electoral), usually by the funeral director. Shipping usually requires the local death certificate, a certificate of embalming and a certificate permitting transfer of the remains; documents for foreign use are legalised via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. A post-mortem is possible for unknown, unnatural, sudden or violent deaths, and a criminal investigation can delay release. Timing depends on circumstances.
PA.authority: Panamanian consulate in the country of death; Ministry of Health (MINSA); Ministry of Foreign Affairs

documents: Death certificate, visaed by the Peruvian consulate (Reglamento DS 03-94-SA, art. 64)
Sanitary transfer authorisation from the country of death, visaed by the Peruvian consulate
Embalming or formolisation certificate signed by a doctor, visaed by the Peruvian consulate (DIRIS requirement when more than 48 h have passed since death)
Forensic autopsy certificate in sudden or violent death
Peruvian sanitary transfer authorisation (DIRIS/DIRESA/GERESA) for onward transfer between health jurisdictions
PE.coffin: Coffins for transport must be impermeable and hermetically closable (DS 03-94-SA art. 39); bodies transferred to another city or country must be in a hermetically sealed coffin, and if the coffin is not watertight the health authority will require a new coffin (art. 62). Zinc lining is not named; confirm the casket with the funeral director and airline.
PE.embalming: Required: bodies transferred to another city or country must be embalmed (DS 03-94-SA art. 62). Burial normally takes place within 48 h of death unless the body has been embalmed with the health authority's authorisation (art. 49).
PE.consular: The Peruvian consulate in the country of death visas the death certificate and the sanitary authorisation (DS 03-94-SA art. 64); DIRIS Lima Centro also requires the embalming or formolisation certificate to be consulate-visaed. A consular representative may apply for the inland transfer authorisation when the deceased was a foreigner with no family in Peru.
PE.arrival: The local funeral home takes over after customs and health clearance. Inland transfer to another health jurisdiction needs a DIRIS/DIRESA/GERESA authorisation (online, fee S/ 62.90 at DIRIS Lima Centro, answer within 2 working days). Burial normally within 48 h of death unless embalmed.
PE.private_aviation: Peruvian law requires remains carried to another city or country to travel in a compartment separate from passengers, and makes the captain responsible (DS 03-94-SA art. 65). Confirm customs and health clearance at the arrival airport before departure.
PE.export: The local undertaker obtains the civil death certificate (temporary, then certified copy after a couple of days), the doctor's death certificate, embalming, a special coffin and the sanitary transfer authorisation from the regional health authority (DIRIS/DIRESA/GERESA). In violent or unclear deaths the prosecutor (Public Ministry) may order a post-mortem and release can be delayed.
PE.authority: Ministry of Health (MINSA) regional authorities DIRIS/DIRESA/GERESA; Peruvian consulates abroad

documents: Death certificate (French translation advisable)
Medical certificate of cause of death / non-contagious disease certificate (confirm with the consulate)
Embalming certificate where required by the departure country
Body transport authorisation from the French embassy or consulate
Coffin sealing report (confirm with the consulate)
PF.coffin: No French Polynesia-specific casket rule was found in the CGCT adaptations, which refer coffin handling to local regulation. Confirm the casket (sealing, lining) with the consulate, the airline and the receiving funeral home.
PF.embalming: No local rule found in the CGCT adaptations; follow the departure country's and airline's requirements and confirm with the receiving funeral home.
PF.consular: French consular services (or the Crisis Centre) can issue an authorisation to transport the body or ashes so the remains leave the foreign country legally. Families pay all costs; the consulate can give an indicative cost and funeral company contacts.
PF.arrival: A local funeral home takes charge of the casket after clearance at the arrival airport (confirm the procedure beforehand). When death occurred outside French Polynesia, burial or cremation must take place no later than the 14th calendar day after the body entered French Polynesia (CGCT art. D2573-16-1).
PF.private_aviation: No official rule specific to private or charter flights carrying human remains was found. The casket is cleared like air cargo: arrive at an international airport with customs, immigration, quarantine and health staff, and have the handling agent and receiving funeral home confirm clearance before departure.
PF.export: Transport of a body or ashes out of French Polynesia is authorised by the High Commissioner of the Republic in French Polynesia (CGCT R. 2213-22 and R. 2213-24 as adapted by art. D2573-16-1). Confirm the documents, casket and the destination's consular rules with the funeral home.
PF.authority: High Commission of the Republic in French Polynesia; French consular network

documents: Original death certificate stating cause of death (apostilled in some posts, e.g. Canberra) plus copies
Notarised mortuary / funeral director certificate: properly embalmed, hermetically sealed casket containing only the deceased
Certificate of no contagious disease from the health authority
Burial transit permit
Passport or ID copies of the deceased; proof of Philippine citizenship and Report of Death for Filipinos
Consignee (receiving Philippine funeral home), carrier, port and flight itinerary
Consular fee and return envelope
PH.coffin: The casket must be hermetically sealed and contain only the deceased. For deaths from a communicable disease, the body must be embalmed, placed in a hermetically sealed metallic casket enclosed in a screwed or nailed wooden case, and disinfected.
PH.embalming: Required: the notarised mortuary certificate must confirm proper embalming (or cremation) under internationally accepted health practices.
PH.consular: The Philippine embassy or consulate issues the Consular Mortuary Certificate. Washington accepts mail applications only, at least 7 working days before the flight (3 to 5 business days processing, 35 USD); Canberra requires the death certificate apostilled and charges 45 AUD for the Report of Death.
PH.arrival: The consignee Philippine funeral home named in the application takes charge of the remains after entry clearance (confirm the procedure with the receiving funeral home). For COVID-19 deaths, remains must be cremated before shipment or the casket kept permanently sealed, with burial within 24 hours of entry clearance (Philippine Embassy Canberra).
PH.private_aviation: No rule specific to private flights was found. The Consular Mortuary Certificate application states the carrier, ports and scheduled arrival, so give the private flight details and carry the originals with the casket; confirm entry clearance at the arrival airport before departure.
PH.export: Leaving the Philippines, the funeral home obtains a certified death certificate, Municipal Transfer Permit, quarantine permit from the Bureau of Quarantine, embalming certificate and fumigation certificate; the remains travel in a hermetically sealed container inside a fumigated wooden crate. Autopsy is mandatory for foreigners when the cause of death cannot be readily determined. A straightforward cremation and repatriation usually takes about 2 to 3 working days to arrange (gov.uk); COVID-19 deaths must be cremated.
PH.authority: Philippine embassy or consulate (Department of Foreign Affairs); Bureau of Quarantine

documents: Death certificate (original and copy)
Passport and/or CNIC/NICOP of the deceased (some missions ask for a notarised copy)
Embalming certificate from the funeral home (most missions, e.g. Houston, Australia)
Certificate that the death was not caused by a communicable disease (most missions)
Burial transit permit (requested by some missions, e.g. Houston)
Letter from the funeral director confirming the certificates (requested by the Australian mission)
Applicant's ID and confirmed flight details for the remains (requested by Birmingham)
NOC for transportation of the dead body issued by the Pakistani mission
PK.coffin: The published mission checklists give no coffin specification. Airlines and the NOC usually expect a hermetically sealed (zinc-lined) coffin in an outer case, but we could not confirm a written official rule. Confirm with the mission and the airline. No official witness of the sealing is mentioned.
PK.embalming: Several Pakistani missions (e.g. Houston, Australia) require an embalming certificate from the funeral home for the NOC; the Birmingham consulate checklist does not list one. Airlines usually expect embalming. Confirm with the mission and the airline.
PK.consular: The Pakistani embassy or consulate covering the place of death issues the NOC. The Birmingham consulate states the service is free and accepts walk-ins without an appointment; Houston works by appointment. Fees and documents differ from mission to mission. The published checklists do not mention apostille or legalisation of the death certificate.
PK.arrival: Customs and health clearance steps for remains at Pakistani airports are not published in the official sources we reviewed. Carry the NOC and all certificates with the coffin and confirm release procedures with the airline or handling agent.
PK.private_aviation: The official sources we reviewed say nothing about private flights carrying remains. Foreign private and charter flights need landing permission from the Pakistan Civil Aviation Authority; confirm the process and timing through your operator. Use an international airport with customs and health staff (e.g. Karachi, Lahore, Islamabad).
PK.export: To take a body out of Pakistan (UK FCDO guidance), you need: the death certificate issued by the local government (a hospital certificate is accepted only if verified by the local police), an embalming certificate, a copy of the passport, and an NOC for repatriation from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. For the UK, you also need a letter from the British High Commission confirming that a UK NOC is not required. Airlines may also ask for a police certificate of no objection, a letter to customs requesting release, a declaration that the coffin contains no restricted items, and the receiving funeral director's details. Post-mortems are done by court-appointed forensic doctors, normally within 24 hours.
PK.authority: Pakistani embassy/consulate (NOC); Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan

documents: Permit (zezwolenie) from the starosta, mayor or city president of the burial district, issued after consulting the district sanitary inspector
Polish consul's certificate (zaświadczenie) allowing the body into Poland
Death certificate (or copy)
Certificate that death was not caused by an infectious disease
Permission to remove the body issued in the country of death
Funeral company declaration that the coffin contains only the remains
PL.coffin: Metal coffin, tightly sealed, with a layer of absorbent material at least 5 cm thick on the bottom, placed in a wooden case so that it cannot move (Polish consulate in Dublin guidance). Who witnesses the sealing abroad is not stated.
PL.embalming: Not mentioned in the official Polish entry guidance; follow the rules of the country of departure.
PL.consular: The Polish consul issues the certificate for bringing the remains into Poland on the basis of the starosta's permit and a copy of the death certificate, at the latest within 3 days of receiving the application and originals (Dublin consulate). The starosta's permit itself carries no stamp duty. Any consular fee is not published on the official pages reviewed; confirm with the consulate. Polish translations were not required by the Dublin consulate. Only the spouse, descendants, ascendants, relatives to the 4th degree and in-laws to the 1st degree may apply.
PL.arrival: Bodies from abroad may only be transported by a specialised funeral company. For deaths from certain infectious diseases (e.g. cholera, plague, rabies, yellow fever) the transfer may only be allowed two years after death.
PL.private_aviation: No rule specific to private aircraft was found. The documents and the sealed metal coffin must accompany the body on any flight; Poland is in Schengen, so a flight from outside Schengen must use an airport with border control.
PL.export: A permit from the competent district (powiatowy) or border state sanitary inspector is required to take a body abroad. It is issued only after documents from the destination and transit countries confirm there is no obstacle to entry or burial. The body must be in a wooden coffin lined with metal or a metal coffin with 5 cm of absorbent material, placed in a sealed wooden crate or other impermeable container; the inspector may require extra precautions and seals the coffin. The death certificate and the deceased's passport are also needed. Permits are not issued for certain infectious diseases until two years after death.
PL.authority: Starosta / mayor of the burial district; Polish consul; State Sanitary Inspection (export)

documents: Death certificate stating the cause of death (with an attested English translation if needed), unless the remains are embalmed or cremated
Embalming certificate where the body is embalmed
Consular Report of Death Abroad or Consular Mortuary Certificate from the US embassy if the deceased was a US citizen
Removal or export permit from the country of departure (as required there)
Passport of the deceased and air waybill or flight manifest (airline requirements)
Name and contact of the receiving licensed funeral home in Puerto Rico
PR.coffin: CDC requires all non-cremated remains to be fully contained in a leak-proof container: a double-layered, puncture-resistant body bag, a lined casket certified leak-proof, or a sealed metal body transfer case. No territorial rule on zinc lining or witnessed sealing was found; the country of departure and the airline may impose a hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin.
PR.embalming: Not required by US federal rules for entry, but embalmed remains are exempt from the CDC death-certificate requirement. Remains of a person who died of certain infectious diseases may need a CDC import permit unless embalmed. Most departure countries and airlines require embalming anyway.
PR.consular: If a US citizen dies abroad, the US embassy or consulate can issue a Consular Report of Death Abroad and, where no death certificate exists, a Consular Mortuary Certificate, Affidavit of Foreign Funeral Director and Transit Permit. A death certificate not in English must come with an English translation attested by a licensed official in the country of death (e.g. a notary).
PR.arrival: Remains are cleared at the first US port of entry, where CDC import requirements apply. Under 42 CFR 71.55 remains for burial or cremation must be consigned directly to a licensed mortuary, cemetery or crematory and, unless embalmed, accompanied by a death certificate (or an importer certification statement). Under Puerto Rico's Funeral Services Act (Law 258-2012), only registered funeral homes and funeral directors may receive a body into Puerto Rico, and the transfer and burial or cremation permit of a person who died outside Puerto Rico serves as proof of death.
PR.pouch: For US/CDC entry purposes, a double-layered, puncture-resistant body bag counts as a leak-proof container. The country of departure, the airline or the aircraft operator may still require a sealed casket or air tray; confirm before the flight.
PR.private_aviation: Human remains on a private or charter flight need the same documents as airline cargo; the documents travel with the coffin and are presented at the arrival airport. The coffin must physically fit the aircraft's cargo door and cargo hold (a coffin never travels in the cabin), which rules out many light and midsize jets; an Embraer Legacy 600 or 650 is usually proposed for an adult casket. An international arrival into Puerto Rico must clear US Customs and Border Protection, so plan the flight to an airport where clearance can be arranged in advance and have the receiving funeral home meet the aircraft. A flight from the US mainland is domestic and needs no customs entry, but the state burial-transit permit should travel with the remains.
PR.export: Under Law 258-2012, a transfer permit (permiso de traslado) is required only when the body leaves Puerto Rico; it is requested by the licensed funeral director from the Demographic Registry (Registro Demografico) or Environmental Health (Salud Ambiental) of the Department of Health, and the body cannot leave before it is issued. Airlines and shipping companies must ask for this permit and for the documents required by the destination. Every body leaving Puerto Rico must be embalmed by a licensed embalmer, except for the US: embalming is not required there if the death certificate shows no contagious or quarantinable disease and the body is in a leak-proof container. For destinations outside the US, the funeral director must contact the destination country's consulate and meet its requirements. Bodies under the Institute of Forensic Sciences cannot be embalmed without its authorisation.
PR.authority: US CDC and CBP (entry); Puerto Rico Department of Health, Demographic Registry and Environmental Health (exit)

documents: From Strasbourg countries: laissez-passer for a corpse from the departure state
From other countries: death registered at the Portuguese consulate and alvara de trasladacao issued by it (for Portuguese nationals)
Death certificate from the country of death
Documents required by the departure country (removal permit, embalming and coffin sealing certificates)
PT.coffin: Strasbourg Agreement standard (Articles 6 and 7): hermetically sealed coffin (typically a soldered zinc inner coffin in a wooden coffin) with absorbent material, containing only the body and personal effects. Confirm the exact specification with the funeral homes and the airline.
PT.embalming: No Portuguese entry rule found; follow the departure country's rules and the airline's requirements.
PT.consular: The consulate covering the place of death transcribes the death into the Portuguese civil register and, at the family's request, issues the alvara de trasladacao. The Consulate-General in London needs no appointment for the alvara; UK certificates need no legalisation or translation there. For ashes in a wooden urn, the airline may require an alvara and consular sealing.
PT.arrival: The receiving Portuguese funeral home collects the coffin at the airport and organises burial with the cemetery. Transport of a body outside the cemetery must be accompanied by the death certificate or a copy of the death record (Decree-Law 5/2000). No burial, cremation or coffin closing before 24 hours after death.
PT.private_aviation: No rule specific to private aircraft was found. Portugal is in Schengen; a flight from outside Schengen must use an airport with border and customs control. The coffin must fit the aircraft's cargo door and cargo hold (a coffin never travels in the cabin), which rules out many light and midsize jets; an Embraer Legacy 600 or 650 is usually proposed for an adult casket.
PT.export: The death is registered at the civil registry; an international death certificate (Certidão de Óbito Internacional) can be requested. For Strasbourg Agreement countries the body travels with a livre-transito mortuario (laissez-passer), issued after checking medical, sanitary, administrative and legal formalities and that the coffin meets Articles 6 and 7 of the Agreement. gov.pt (April 2026) names the Public Prosecution (Ministerio Publico) as issuer, while Decree-Law 5/2000 gives this to the GNR and PSP police, so confirm the issuer locally. A post-mortem, if needed, normally takes place within 3 to 4 working days; cremation may need the public prosecutor's permission.
PT.authority: Portuguese consulates (alvara de trasladacao); Ministerio Publico / police (livre-transito for exit); cemetery administration

Validated death certificate
Post-mortem report, if one was carried out, and any other documents the mission requests
Embalming certificate and certificate of hermetic sealing (airline and departure-country requirement; confirm with the mission)
Air waybill with flight date and time
QA.coffin: No Qatari import standard is published. Use a hermetically sealed casket in an outer case meeting airline requirements; confirm with the Qatari mission.
QA.embalming: Remains leaving Qatar must have an embalming and sealing certificate (gov.uk). Incoming embalming rules are not published; confirm with the Qatari mission.
QA.consular: Qatari embassy or consulate (for Qatari citizens): notified of the death by relatives, collects the original passport and validated death documents, sends copies of the passport, death certificate and post-mortem report to Doha, and notifies the Department of Consular Affairs of the date and time of the flight for airport arrangements. No fee is published for this service. Qatar is not a party to the Strasbourg Agreement.
QA.arrival: For Qatari citizens, the Department of Consular Affairs makes arrangements with the airport once the mission gives the flight date and time. For other cases no official arrival procedure is published; confirm customs clearance and collection with the airline or handling agent and the receiving funeral service. Cremation is not possible in Qatar.
QA.private_aviation: No official rule specific to private or charter flights carrying human remains was found. Because the Department of Consular Affairs coordinates airport arrangements, give the mission the exact arrival time and airport before take-off. Regional tensions in 2026: UK FCDO warns of possible flight cancellations and airspace closures in the Middle East at short notice (advice updated 27 Oct 2026).
QA.export: The hospital or Ministry of Public Health issues the notification of death. The Humanitarian Services Office near Hamad Hospital mortuary (Public Health and Ministry of Interior desks, plus a Qatar Airways representative) issues the death certificate and the transfer of dead body certificate, free of charge. A police letter is needed in police cases. The home embassy issues its NOC (Pakistan Embassy: same day). Immigration and customs clearance are done at the Qatar Airways cargo terminal; the ambulance takes the body from the mortuary to cargo at flight time. An embalming and sealing certificate is issued for bodies leaving Qatar. Cremation is not possible.

In practice this is a soldered zinc lining inside a wooden coffin; confirm the specification with the funeral director.
RE.embalming: The official French pages reviewed do not set an embalming requirement for an incoming body; follow the departure country's and the airline's rules.
RE.consular: From abroad, entry into France (including overseas departments) and transport to the place of burial or cremation require authorisation from the French embassy or consulate. France is a party to the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement; whether a Strasbourg laissez-passer alone suffices for this department is not stated, confirm with the consulate. Families bear all costs.
RE.arrival: The receiving funeral director takes the coffin at the airport. Confirm the counting with the local funeral director.
RE.private_aviation: Same documents as airline cargo; the coffin must be airtight for any air transport. Plan arrival at Roland Garros (Saint-Denis) international airport, with customs (douane) and border police, and have the receiving funeral director meet the aircraft.
RE.export: The funeral company handles formalities. To mainland France or abroad, the prefect of the department where the coffin is closed authorises the transport; air transport requires an airtight coffin. Ashes need authorisation from the prefect of the place of cremation or of the applicant's residence. The destination country's consular rules also apply.

Embalming certificate
Receipt declaration from the administration of the cemetery in Romania where the burial will take place
Identity document of the deceased
RO.coffin: Romania's mortuary passport model (HG 741/2016, annex 7) states the special condition: metal coffin, hermetically closed, then placed in a tightly closed wooden box. Confirm sealing requirements with the Romanian consulate and the airline.
RO.embalming: Romanian rules make embalming mandatory when a body is transported for burial to a place at least 30 km away (HG 741/2016 art. 5), and the mortuary passport for export is issued on the basis of the embalming certificate (art. 32). Plan embalming in the departure country and confirm with the consulate. Embalming is forbidden before a judicial autopsy and for highly pathogenic infectious diseases.
RO.consular: The approval of the Romanian consular office in the country of death is one of the three approvals required under Law 102/2014 art. 29(2); in practice the Romanian consulate issues a mortuary passport for the transport to Romania. The family or the funeral company applies. The consular pages (mae.ro) could not be opened to confirm the document list and fees; confirm with the consulate.
RO.arrival: The Romanian funeral home receives the coffin; the receiving cemetery's declaration must be obtained beforehand. Detailed customs and health clearance steps on arrival are not published in the sources reviewed.
RO.private_aviation: No rule specific to private aircraft found. Use an airport with border and customs control and carry the mortuary passport with the coffin.
RO.export: Leaving Romania: international transport is made on a 'pasaport pentru transport cadavru uman' (model in annex 7 of HG 741/2016), issued by the public health directorate (DSP) of the county where the death or exhumation occurred, on the basis of the death certificate and the embalming certificate. The coffin is a hermetically closed metal coffin in a tightly closed wooden case, and transport abroad must comply with international conventions. UK FCDO lists the documents needed: notice of death certificate, international death certificate, mortuary passport, authorisation for international transport and embalming certificate. Post mortems are usually done within 24 hours.
RO.authority: Romanian embassy/consulate in the country of death (approval, mortuary passport); county public health directorates (DSP) for export

Certificate of no contagious disease (required by the Oslo embassy)
Confirmation of a burial place in Serbia (for foreign nationals, or if no Serbian passport)
RS.coffin: Not stated on the Serbian consular checklists. Serbian practice is a sealed coffin with a soldered metal container inside a wooden coffin (US Embassy Belgrade for export); plan a hermetically sealed zinc-lined casket meeting airline rules.
RS.embalming: An embalming certificate is listed by the Serbian Embassy in Athens; plan embalming in the country of departure. In Serbia embalming is available only in Belgrade and Novi Sad (Forensic Institutes).
RS.consular: The Serbian diplomatic mission covering the place of death issues the sprovodnica on presentation of original documents (death certificate apostilled; Athens and Oslo also require a Serbian translation). Documents can be pre-checked by email, then an appointment is booked to collect the permit (Oslo). Fee per the consular price list. If death was caused by plague or smallpox, the mission obtains Ministry of Health approval before issuing. A transit sprovodnica is needed if the body only crosses Serbia.
RS.arrival: A Serbian funeral home collects the casket; customs clearance procedures on arrival are not detailed in the official sources reviewed, so confirm with the airline or handling agent. The death of a Serbian citizen abroad is also registered with the Serbian civil registry (registration form via the consulate). For deaths in Serbia burial must take place between 24 and 72 hours after death, extendable in some cases, particularly if refrigerated.
RS.private_aviation: No specific rules published for private flights carrying remains. The consulate's request asks for the transport method and flight number, so the sprovodnica should name the private flight. Use an international airport with customs (e.g. Belgrade or Nis).
RS.export: Leaving Serbia (US Embassy Belgrade): the official Serbian death certificate on the international form and a customs declaration from the local Customs Administration office, attached to the outside of the container. The body is placed in a sealed coffin with a metal container. Embalming only in Belgrade and Novi Sad (about USD 1,300; about USD 2,000 including the doctor's certification). Autopsy may be ordered by the Public Prosecutor (up to 4 working days). Burial must take place within 72 hours, extendable in some cases, particularly if refrigerated.
RS.authority: Serbian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and its missions (sprovodnica); Ministry of Health (infectious cases); Customs Administration

RU.coffin: Hermetically soldered metal (zinc) coffin packed in a wooden box, bearing the wax seals of the institutions that issued the certificates (customs instruction of 22 July 1992; still listed, status not confirmed by an official consolidated source).
RU.embalming: Not required by the published customs rule; normally done in the country of departure for international transport.
RU.consular: For import and transit, the sanitary and no-contents certificates are issued or certified by Russian diplomatic missions abroad. Documents need translation into Russian and apostille or legalisation.
RU.arrival: Customs clears the coffin only with the certificates and intact seals. A Russian funeral company receives the casket.
RU.private_aviation: Russia closed its airspace to aircraft from many countries (including EU, UK, US and Canada) and those states closed theirs to Russian aircraft. A private flight must use an official border crossing airport with customs and sanitary-quarantine control and must comply with sanctions.
RU.export: Leaving Russia: official death certificate from ZAGS (apostilled, translated), certificate of encasement (sealed, no foreign objects) from the funeral company, medical certificate from the Forensic Bureau confirming absence of contagious disease, plus the destination consulate's documents. RW.coffin: The Rwandan mission pages do not specify casket requirements. Follow the airline's requirements (usually a hermetically sealed inner container in a wooden outer coffin) and confirm with the mission.
RW.embalming: Embalming is required: every Rwandan mission page consulted lists a certificate of embalming.
RW.consular: The Rwandan embassy or high commission in the country of death issues the body repatriation document or burial permit. The Ottawa mission processes it free of charge in up to 3 business days; Washington charges 30 USD and Doha 40 QR. Incomplete applications are returned.
RW.arrival: No official description of arrival clearance at Kigali was found. Carry the mission document and originals with the coffin; a relative or funeral home in Rwanda collects it.
RW.private_aviation: No rule specific to private flights was found. Land at an international airport with customs and health control (Kigali International) with the mission document travelling with the coffin.
RW.export: For a body leaving Rwanda, UK guidance says a local death certificate, a certificate of embalming and a certificate giving permission to transfer the body are always required. Local formalities normally take three or four days for a natural death; police investigation of sudden or suspicious deaths can delay release. Medical certificate or other evidence of name, date and cause of death and the preservation measures used (required for approval of repatriations)
Death certificate (translation requirements to confirm with the Public Health Authority)
Embalming certificate
Exit permit from the country of death
Passport of the deceased
SC.coffin: No specification published. A casket containing human remains brought into Seychelles must not be opened without the Commissioner's written approval. Plan for a hermetically sealed zinc-lined inner coffin in a wooden outer case.
SC.embalming: No explicit entry rule, but a request for approval of a repatriation must describe the measures adopted to preserve the remains; embalming is the usual measure. Confirm with the Public Health Authority.
SC.consular: Approval comes from the Public Health Commissioner (Public Health Authority), not from consulates; the receiving undertaker can help reach the Authority. The Minister may also restrict or prohibit entry of corpses or ashes from specified countries by regulation (s. 26). Not a party to the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement.
SC.arrival: Clearance at Seychelles International Airport (Mahé) with the Commissioner's written approval; a local undertaker receives the coffin. Opening the casket requires a separate written approval. Bringing in remains without approval or opening the casket is an offence (fine up to SCR 50,000 or 2 years' imprisonment).
SC.private_aviation: Section 27 applies to any carriage, including private flights: the written approval of the Public Health Commissioner must be held before the remains are brought in. A private flight should land at Seychelles International Airport with customs and health control and carry the approval and all originals.
SC.export: Exit also needs the Public Health Commissioner's written approval (s. 27 Public Health Act 2015): request it in writing with a medical certificate giving the name, date and cause of death and preservation measures, at least 48 hours before embalming and repatriation. UK guidance says local formalities can take seven days or more; the undertaker handles embalming and documents, and the passport and all original documents (post-mortem and police reports) travel with the body. Ashes need a Public Health Authority letter.
SC.authority: Public Health Commissioner, Public Health Authority (Ministry of Health), Seychelles

SD.coffin: No official specification found. Plan for a hermetically sealed inner container in a wooden outer coffin as required by airlines.
SD.embalming: Not stated in the Sudanese embassy checklist. Families may prefer to avoid embalming for Islamic burial; ask the embassy and airline what is accepted.
SD.consular: Submit the file to the Sudanese embassy or consulate in the country of death at least 48 hours before the flight (Embassy in The Hague). Fees are not published. The death certificate must be legalised by the local foreign ministry.
SD.arrival: No official arrival procedure was found. UK travel advice says Khartoum and Port Sudan airports operate limited flights and have been targeted by drone strikes. Islamic burial is normally held quickly; arrange the receiving family in advance.
SD.private_aviation: Khartoum and Port Sudan airports operate limited flights and may close after drone strikes. A private flight needs overflight and landing permission and current security information.
SD.export: UK guidance (2021): deaths are registered at the district health office and the death certificate is issued in Arabic; embalming is required for repatriation, and the local undertaker needs a permission letter signed and stamped by the destination country's embassy. documents: Death certificate from the competent authority or doctor in the country of death, stating the date and, if possible, the cause of death
Laissez-passer for the corpse from the departure country (Strasbourg Agreement parties) or that country's transport documents
Application for a burial or cremation permit to the Swedish Police Authority (Polismyndigheten)
SE.coffin: Under the Strasbourg Agreement: an impervious coffin with absorbent material, either an outer wooden coffin with walls at least 20 mm thick and a soldered zinc inner coffin, or a single wooden coffin at least 30 mm thick lined with zinc or another self-destroying material; for air transport a purifying device or adequate pressure resistance. Sealing is certified by the departure country's authorities.
SE.embalming: Not required for transport. In Sweden embalming is required only before burial in a church, burial vault or similar space.
SE.consular: Under the Strasbourg Agreement the destination state may not require documents other than the laissez-passer (apart from general transport documents). For countries outside the Agreement, confirm with the Swedish embassy; translation of the foreign death certificate may be requested.
SE.arrival: The Police Authority grants the burial or cremation permit for a body brought into Sweden, sends it to the Tax Agency (Skatteverket) and forwards the foreign death certificate to the National Board of Health and Welfare. A funeral should if possible take place within a month of death.
SE.private_aviation: No Swedish rule specific to private aircraft found. Swedish rules for air transport of coffins require a pressure-equalising device or a coffin able to withstand pressure changes. Sweden is in Schengen; a flight from outside Schengen must use an airport with border and customs control.
SE.export: A body may only leave Sweden with a passersedel (laissez-passer) issued by the Swedish Tax Agency (Skatteverket), which must accompany the body. It is issued once a burial or cremation certificate can be issued and an undertaker certifies the coffin meets the rules and contains only the body and personal effects (not required for Nordic destinations). The form is in Swedish and English or French. The coffin must be moisture-proof with absorbent lining: wooden outer coffin (2 cm) with zinc inner coffin, or 3 cm wooden coffin lined with zinc; for air transport a pressure-equalising device. Infectious deaths require a shroud soaked in antiseptic. A copy of the passersedel certifying export must be returned to Skatteverket within two weeks. Documents commonly provided: death certificate, non-contagious certificate, embalming certificate, freight certificate and soldering (sealing) certificate.
SE.authority: Swedish Police Authority (entry burial permit); Swedish Tax Agency, Skatteverket (export laissez-passer)

SG.coffin: A sealing certificate for the coffin is required (NEA). Singapore MFA's 2021 guide described it as certifying that the coffin is hermetically sealed and metal-lined. For burial in Singapore the coffin must not exceed 210 x 90 x 80 cm; Singapore cremators accept coffins only up to 210 x 60 x 56 cm, so size the coffin for the planned disposal. Who witnesses the sealing is not specified by Singapore.
SG.embalming: An embalming certificate is required 'where applicable' (NEA). Tell the embalmer about any pacemaker. For infectious diseases of concern (e.g. MERS, Ebola) both undertakers must notify the authorities, and NEA Port Health decides whether the body may be imported at all.
SG.consular: No Singapore consular permit or laissez-passer is needed; the import permit is issued by NEA, not by Singapore embassies. MFA and Singapore overseas missions only assist and provide undertaker lists. Documents not in English need an English translation; legalisation is not mentioned by NEA.
SG.arrival: No Singapore Customs permit or GST applies to human remains or ashes. The Singapore funeral director collects the coffin. The Permit to Bury or Cremate is issued with the coffin permit (fee 17.50 SGD). Burials take place only at Choa Chu Kang Cemetery, with a 15-year grave lease; foreigners cremated in Singapore can only buy niches in private columbaria.
SG.private_aviation: Singapore has no published rule specific to private flights carrying remains. SG.export: A coffin permit for export is issued by NEA (Port Health) and applied for online through NEA's e-services, normally by the funeral director. Confirm the supporting documents (usually the death certificate, embalming certificate where applicable and coffin sealing certificate) with the funeral director or NEA Port Health Office. In coroner's cases the body is released only after the Coroner's decision on autopsy; a provisional cause of death ('Cardiorespiratory Failure Pending Further Investigations') may be used to allow repatriation. Processing time is not published.
SG.authority: National Environment Agency (NEA), Port Health Office

SI.coffin: Rules on the transport and burial of human remains (Uradni list RS 53/2017, art. 5): impermeable coffin containing absorbent material, either an outer wooden coffin with sides at least 20 mm thick and a hermetically sealed inner coffin of zinc or other self-decomposing material, or a single wooden coffin at least 30 mm thick lined with zinc or similar. Infectious-disease deaths: body also wrapped in a shroud soaked in antiseptic.
SI.embalming: Not addressed by the Slovenian rules; embalming is not compulsory in Slovenia but can be requested, especially when repatriation is planned (gov.uk).
SI.consular: Slovenian rules (art. 6) require every body brought into Slovenia to travel with a corpse passport issued by the competent authority of the departure country; between Strasbourg Agreement parties no other documents may be required. From a non-party country, confirm with the Slovenian embassy or consulate what is accepted. Urns do not need a corpse passport.
SI.arrival: On arrival the coffin is collected by a Slovenian funeral service provider (pogrebna dejavnost). Remains of a person who died of an infectious disease must be cremated or buried in the transport coffin. Cremation is available only in Ljubljana.
SI.private_aviation: No rule specific to private aircraft found. The coffin must be carried in a space separate from passengers and baggage (art. 4). Slovenia is in Schengen; a flight from outside Schengen must use an airport with border and customs control.
SI.export: Leaving Slovenia: the corpse passport is issued by the Health Inspectorate of the Republic of Slovenia (Zdravstveni inspektorat RS) on application by the funeral provider with the death notification completed by the medical examiner, a copy of the identity document and the provider's written statement that the coffin complies and contains only the deceased. It is written in Slovenian and one official EU language; the cause of death is given with the WHO ICD code. UK guidance adds that permission to remove the body is issued by a coroner and obtained by the funeral director. Slovenian death certificates do not state the cause of death; an international multilingual version can be requested. Embalming is optional.
SI.authority: Health Inspectorate of the Republic of Slovenia (Zdravstveni inspektorat RS); Ministry of Health

From non-party states: corpse passport (pas pre mŕtvolu) issued by the Slovak embassy or consulate
Death certificate
Documents required by the country of departure
SK.coffin: The coffin must meet the requirements of the Strasbourg Agreement: impervious, with absorbent material, a soldered zinc inner coffin in a wooden outer coffin (or a zinc-lined wooden coffin at least 30 mm thick). The coffin label must carry the deceased's identity.
SK.embalming: Not required by Slovak law for entry. Embalming, preservation and display of the body are prohibited when the person was infected with a dangerous disease at the time of death.
SK.consular: From a state not bound by the agreement, the Slovak diplomatic mission or consulate issues the corpse passport if all requirements of the departure state are met and the coffin meets the agreement's requirements (Act 131/2010 Coll. section 7(3)).
SK.arrival: Slovak funeral services, crematoria and embalmers may accept the remains on the basis of the corpse passport for international transport. Road transport in Slovakia must use a refrigerated hearse.
SK.private_aviation: No rule specific to private aircraft found. Slovakia is in Schengen; a flight from outside Schengen must use an airport with border and customs control.
SK.export: Within Strasbourg countries, transport follows the agreement. The corpse passport (laissez-passer) is issued by the self-governing region (samosprávny kraj), by the regional public health authority if the deceased had a dangerous infectious disease, or by the Health Care Surveillance Authority if an autopsy was performed (Act 131/2010 section 7(4)). SL.private_aviation: UK guidance states that Brussels Airlines is the only commercial airline from Sierra Leone currently carrying human remains, with limited flights, so commercial repatriation can take several weeks. Authorisation of the Ufficiale di Stato Civile - Dirigente la Polizia Mortuaria, issued after clearance (nulla osta) by the health services
SM.coffin: San Marino's coffin rules (Law 35/2010, Annex 4): zinc inner coffin at least 0.660 mm thick, hermetically closed by continuous soldering, inside a solid wooden coffin at least 25 mm thick. SM.embalming: No San Marino entry rule found; follow the departure country's and Italy's transit rules.
SM.consular: No San Marino consular procedure is published. San Marino is not a party to the Strasbourg Agreement. Confirm with the San Marino civil registry and with the Italian consulate whether Italian transit documents are needed.
SM.arrival: Customs clearance takes place at the Italian arrival airport (Rimini or Bologna). A funeral vehicle must carry the coffin; transport within San Marino and burial need the authorisation of the civil registrar (Dirigente la Polizia Mortuaria), issued after the health services' clearance.
SM.private_aviation: San Marino has no airport. Land in Italy (Rimini or Bologna are the nearest airports), where Italian customs and health rules apply, then transfer by funeral vehicle. SM.export: Transport out of San Marino follows the international conventions San Marino has joined, or otherwise the rules of the departure and destination states; the civil registrar authorises it after the health services' clearance. For foreign burial, cremation or ventilated tombs a wooden coffin alone is allowed; where a metal coffin is needed it must be zinc (at least 0.660 mm). SM.authority: Ufficiale di Stato Civile - Dirigente la Polizia Mortuaria; San Marino health services (nulla osta); Italian authorities for transit

SN.consular: Senegalese consulates (for France, the Consulate General in Paris) issue the laissez-passer mortuaire, often in liaison with the funeral home chosen by the family. SN.arrival: No official description of arrival clearance at Dakar Blaise Diagne airport was found. Burial usually follows quickly; arrange a receiving funeral home or family member in advance. Cremation is not available in Senegal.
SN.private_aviation: The Senegalese consulate's checklist asks for the itinerary of the remains 'travelling as freight' to Senegal. No rule specific to private flights was found. A private flight should land at an international airport with customs and health control (normally Dakar Blaise Diagne) with all originals travelling with the coffin.
SN.export: UK government guidance for taking a body out of Senegal lists a civil registry death certificate (in French), permission to remove the body issued by a coroner, the passport, a certificate of cause of death, a certificate of non-contagiousness, a burial permit from the town hall, a police report, an authorisation from the Ministry of Interior, a transportation certificate and a certificate of embalming. Cremation is not available in Senegal. From France: the funeral company files the request; the transport is authorised by the préfet of the département where the coffin is closed, and a hermetic metal-lined coffin is mandatory for air transport (service-public.gouv.fr). The prefecture may also ask for a certificate of non-epidemic (CNE) issued by the regional health agency (ARS), which some countries not party to the 1937 Berlin agreement require; confirm with the prefecture.
SN.authority: Senegalese consulates abroad (laissez-passer mortuaire); Ministry of Interior for bodies leaving Senegal

SS.embalming: Not published for entry; expected for international air transport. For remains leaving South Sudan, embalming is required and done by a private pathologist at Juba Teaching Hospital.

SS.arrival: No official information on clearance at Juba International Airport was found. Refrigerated storage is scarce (UNMISS mortuary, Juba Funeral Home); arrange the receiving family or funeral home in advance. Transport outside Juba is difficult and a charter may be needed.
SS.private_aviation: UK travel advice warns that Juba airport may close or be inaccessible and flights can be cancelled at short notice; South Sudan's airspace has closed temporarily in the past. SS.export: UK bereavement pack: a senior medical officer at Juba Teaching Hospital certifies the death; the Ministry of Health issues the death certificate and burial permit in English, stating the cause of death. Embalming is required for international transport and is done by a private pathologist at Juba Teaching Hospital, who issues the embalming and non-infectiousness certificates (family pays). Caskets for international air travel are not available in Juba and must be imported, for example from Kenya. The death certificate generally takes a few working days.
SS.authority: Embassy of the Republic of South Sudan in the country of death; South Sudan Ministry of Health

TG.coffin: The Togolese embassy in Berlin asks for the municipal authorisation to close the coffin but publishes no technical specification. Airlines and departure countries generally require a hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin in a wooden case; confirm with the embassy.
TG.embalming: Embalming is required: an embalming certificate is part of the embassy file.
TG.consular: The Togolese embassy covering the country of death issues the authorisation to transfer the body (Berlin: 50 EUR normal, 70 EUR express, file due at least 8 days before transfer). TG.private_aviation: No published rule specific to private or charter flights was found. TG.export: Leaving Togo requires an authorisation to transfer remains (arrete de sortie) from the Ministry of Security in Lome: death certificate, cause-of-death or non-contagion certificate from the hospital, ID of the deceased and of the applicant, 500 FCFA fiscal stamp, online application on service-public.gouv.tg, processed in 72 hours and collected in person. TG.authority: Togolese embassy abroad (entry); Ministry of Security, Lome (transfer authorisation)

Hospital letter confirming death and local death certificate
Passport of the deceased
Air waybill (original or copy)

TH.coffin: No Thai-specific casket standard was found in official sources. Use the casket required by the country of departure and the airline (usually hermetically sealed); confirm with the funeral director and airline.
TH.embalming: Not specified by Thai official sources for incoming remains; normally required by the country of departure and by airlines.
TH.consular: Royal Thai embassies state that the process must be handled by a funeral director; the embassy issues the Thai death certificate used to send the body to Thailand. Legalisation of the foreign death certificate may be required depending on the post.
TH.arrival: Thai Customs at the airport (e.g. Suvarnabhumi, Don Mueang) check the documents, release the remains and record them; the importer signs a pick-up document. No Import Declaration or Special Declaration form is required.
TH.private_aviation: No Thai rule specific to private flights was found. Remains are cleared by Customs at the arrival airport on the same documents; arrange customs clearance and handling in advance.
TH.export: Non-hospital deaths are reported to the police; the death is registered at the district office (amphur), which issues a Thai-language certificate. The UK FCDO notes a letter from the deceased's embassy may be needed for the hospital or authorities to release the body. Post-mortems are normally required for non-Thai nationals. Local funeral directors provide the death certificate, a certificate of embalming and a certificate permitting transfer. At the airport, Customs need originals and two copies of the death documents, passport, the destination embassy's certificate for return of remains and the air waybill; no export declaration form. No official overall delay is published.
TH.authority: Royal Thai Embassy or consulate; Thai Customs Department

TJ.coffin: Not published officially for entry; confirm with the Tajik consulate. For bodies leaving Tajikistan, the UK FCDO states an airproof, sealed zinc coffin is required.
TJ.embalming: Not published officially for incoming bodies; confirm with the Tajik consulate. Embalming is mandatory for repatriation from Tajikistan (UK FCDO).
TJ.consular: Tajikistan is not a party to the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement. Contact the Tajik embassy or consulate in the country of death about consular certification, legalisation or apostille and Tajik or Russian translations.
TJ.arrival: Not published officially; confirm customs and sanitary clearance at the arrival airport with the Tajik consulate and the receiving funeral service. Cremation is not available in Tajikistan.
TJ.private_aviation: No official rule specific to human remains on private aircraft was found. Plan arrival at an international airport with customs, border and sanitary-quarantine control, and have the handling agent confirm clearance of the coffin in advance.
TJ.export: The civil registry (ZAGS) issues the death certificate in Tajik and Russian within 1 to 3 days of the medical certificate of death. In sudden deaths the prosecutor or criminal police issue a report before release; criminal investigations can delay release. According to the UK FCDO, repatriation needs embalming, an airproof sealed zinc coffin delivered to the airport cargo terminal at least 4 hours before the flight, the death certificate, permission to remove the body issued by a coroner, a funeral director's letter that no foreign objects were in the coffin with a list of accompanying items, and a Health Inspection Services certificate. TJ.authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Tajikistan (consular department); Health Inspection Services and ZAGS for exit

Documents required by the country of death to export the body
Passport of the deceased
Any further certificates requested by the Turkmen consulate (e.g. embalming, sealing)
TM.coffin: Not published officially for entry; confirm the casket requirements with the Turkmen consulate and the airline. For repatriation from Turkmenistan, the UK FCDO says a special casket is arranged through the local funeral director.
TM.embalming: Not published officially; confirm with the Turkmen consulate and the airline.
TM.consular: Turkmenistan is not a party to the 1973 Strasbourg Agreement. For a foreign citizen to be buried in Turkmenistan, local authorities must give special permission, requested through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
TM.arrival: Not published officially. Expect customs and sanitary clearance at the arrival airport (normally Ashgabat) and handover to a local funeral service. There are no cremation facilities in Turkmenistan.
TM.private_aviation: No official rule specific to human remains on private aircraft was found. Plan arrival at an international airport with customs, border and sanitary-quarantine control, and have the handling agent confirm clearance of the coffin in advance.
TM.export: The civil registry (ZAGS) issues the death certificate in Turkmen, recording the cause of death, within a few days; a consular officer may need to be present. If the cause is still being investigated, the certificate may be delayed. Leaving Turkmenistan requires a letter of repatriation from the local Prosecutor's Office confirming no signs of violent or suspicious death, and the Turkmen death certificate. TN.coffin: No Tunisian text on coffin specifications for international transport was found. Use the casket required by the country of death and the airline (usually hermetically sealed); confirm with the consulate.
TN.embalming: Not required by any Tunisian text found. The country of departure or the airline may require it; confirm with the consulate and the carrier.
TN.consular: For a Tunisian who dies abroad, the Tunisian embassy or consulate with jurisdiction over the place of death issues the transport permit for entry into Tunisia (Ministry of Interior service sheet). The e-consulat list also includes an Arabic death extract. For a foreign national to be buried in Tunisia, no official procedure was found; ask the Tunisian consulate.

Cremation is not allowed in Tunisia.
TN.private_aviation: No Tunisian rule specific to remains on private aircraft was found. Land at an international airport with customs and health services and have the handling agent arrange release of the coffin with the consular permit and documents.
TN.export: Leaving Tunisia: the death must be registered at the municipality within 72 hours (French version of the certificate available; it does not show the cause of death). TR.embalming: Required: Turkish consulates ask for an embalming certificate before issuing the transfer document.
TR.consular: The Turkish consulate in the country of death issues the Cenaze Nakil Belgesi free of charge, on application by a relative or authorised person or by the funeral company, in person or by post (practice varies by post). TR.arrival: Documents travel with the coffin. The coffin is cleared at the arrival airport and released to the family or the funeral service. There is no cremation in Turkey.
TR.private_aviation: No rule specific to remains on private aircraft was found. The laissez-passer or consular transfer document and the death and embalming certificates must travel with the coffin, and the handling agent must arrange customs clearance at an international airport.
TR.export: Leaving Turkey requires the Formul C multilingual death certificate from the civil registry (or the hospital death report if not yet issued), an embalming certificate and permission to transfer the body. In unnatural or unexplained deaths the prosecutor and forensic medicine are involved and a post-mortem is usually done within 1 to 3 days. For Strasbourg Agreement destinations an international laissez-passer is issued. Cremation is not legal in Turkey.
TR.authority: Turkish consulate abroad (Ministry of Foreign Affairs); civil registry and public prosecutor for exit

TT.consular: The nearest Trinidad and Tobago mission (or honorary consul, or the local foreign ministry where there is none) certifies the original documents and sends them to the Consular Affairs Division in Port of Spain, which obtains the Ministry of Health and Ministry of Homeland Security approvals. TT.private_aviation: Approvals must be in hand before the flight is confirmed; most airlines require them and a private operator should too. The casket clears through the Customs and Excise Division at the port of entry with the receiving funeral home.
TT.export: Leaving Trinidad and Tobago: register the death with the District Registrar (certificate usually within a week, longer if police investigate). TW.coffin: No Taiwanese casket specification found. Use the casket required by the country of death and the airline; confirm with the receiving funeral home.
TW.embalming: No official Taiwanese rule found; the country of death or the airline may require it. Confirm with the funeral homes.
TW.consular: Not confirmed. Ask Taiwan's representative office abroad (TECO) whether legalisation of the death certificate is needed.
TW.arrival: Quarantine by the Taiwan CDC quarantine unit at the port of entry under the Regulations Governing Quarantine at Ports (Article 26), then customs clearance and collection by a funeral home. Deaths from a communicable disease follow the Communicable Disease Control Act.
TW.private_aviation: The death certificate must be presented to the quarantine unit at the port of entry wherever the aircraft lands. No other rule specific to private flights found.
TW.export: The same rule applies on departure: the remains and the death certificate (or other document stating the cause of death) must be presented to the quarantine unit. Ashes and bones are exempt. Other export documents depend on the destination country.

TZ.coffin: The Tanzanian missions' published checklists do not specify casket construction. Use the casket required by the country of death and the airline (usually hermetically sealed); confirm with the mission and the airline. No published rule on who witnesses the sealing.
TZ.embalming: Embalming is required: the missions ask for a notarised embalming certificate.
TZ.consular: Send the documents to the Tanzanian embassy or high commission covering the country of death (e.g. Washington; Brussels files go via the High Commission in Nairobi per the Brussels page).
